titleZh: 黄金周过后，客流下降，酒店节能措施升级了吗？
titleEn: After Golden Week, When Guest Traffic Falls, Have Your Hotel’s Energy-Saving Measures Improved?
summaryZh: 客流回落后，酒店应把营业需求传递到设备运行安排，明确调整、恢复与验证责任。用一份七项运行调整单，核对节能效果并守住服务条件。
summaryEn: When guest demand falls, connect actual operating requirements to equipment schedules. A seven-entry adjustment sheet clarifies changes, restoration and verification while protecting service.
contentZh:
黄金周过后，客流下降，酒店节能措施升级了吗？

黄金周接待高峰过后，如果本店入住间夜、餐饮人数或会议活动开始回落，总经理值得问一问：营业量变了，酒店的用能安排跟着变了吗？

节能措施有没有升级，先看运行管理。哪些区域仍有客人使用，哪些设备还按高峰时段启动，谁负责调整，需求回来后怎样恢复，都应有明确安排。电费下降可以作为检查入口，却不能单独证明措施有效；换了一套设备，也不代表运行方式已经改善。

客人少了，设备未必跟着少开

酒店用能不只跟客房入住有关。早餐、宴会、会议、洗涤及公共区域各有运行需求。同样的入住间夜，餐饮人数或会议时段不同，整店用电也可能不同。部分系统还需要维持必要运行，不能因为空房增加就同比例削减。

假设一家酒店节后客房需求回落，会议厅却仍有连续活动。如果只按入住率要求全店压电量，可能把有业务需求的区域一起压缩。反过来，没有会议的厅室仍按原有时间提前开灯、开空调，也可能存在可以核对的运行浪费。这个例子用于说明检查方法，不对应任何真实门店。

总经理应先让客房、餐饮和会议负责人报出实际使用需求，再由工程核对设备运行记录。需求变化没有传到设备安排上，节能就容易停留在“大家注意随手关灯”的提醒层面。

先调整运行，再讨论投入

美国环保署ENERGY STAR的商业建筑节能清单，把检查非营业时段仍在运行的设备、优化启停时间及设备运行顺序列为低成本措施；其运行维护建议也强调复核定时和其他控制设置。借鉴的是检查思路，具体设备怎样调整，仍须符合本店系统条件。

对有独立控制条件的会议厅，可以先核对活动结束后照明、空调的实际运行时段；对后勤区域，可以核对非工作时段的普通照明是否按安排关闭。不要只查控制器上写了什么，还要到现场看实际状态。计时器设定、员工操作和设备运行不一致时，新增节能设备未必能解决问题。

调整前要把权限和边界说清楚。普通照明与应急照明分开核对；空调、新风、热水等系统由工程负责人评估运行需要，不交给各部门自行停启。是否适合降低负荷或缩短运行时间，取决于系统设计、通风、环境维护、服务承诺及当地要求。集中系统不一定能按单个房间或区域独立调整，不能照搬分区设备的做法。

需要更换设备或改控制系统时，再由工程提出技术依据，财务核对全口径投入，业主决定预算。没有摸清运行偏差，就先采购一套“节能方案”，可能把低成本可解决的问题变成新投资。

一份能落实到现场的运行调整单

第一次节后经营会，可以先选一个具备独立控制条件、风险较低的区域，填写以下七项。它用于组织检查，不是要求全店同时停用设备。

区域与设备：写到可识别的位置和设备，标明是否独立控制、由哪块表计量；不能只写“会议区域节能”。

实际需求：由使用部门填活动时段、准备时间及需要保持的服务条件。工程不能只拿预订计划当实际使用记录，也要核对临时增加的活动。

原有运行：记下实际启停时间和控制方式，区分人工操作与自动控制。没有记录时先补测，不凭印象填一个“原来全天开”。

拟议调整：工程明确改哪项设置、为什么可以改、哪些设备不动。一次试查尽量只改变一项主要安排，便于解释结果。

执行与恢复：写明执行人、批准人、恢复正常运行所需时间，以及新增预订或临时活动如何传达。节能不能靠临时找人开门、开机才能恢复服务。

验证资料：列出对应电量、使用时段、天气、现场状态、服务问题及恢复所需资源。没有分表时，应注明整店数据还混有其他业务负荷。

撤回与复盘：写清什么现象出现就恢复原安排、谁有权立即处理，以及何时查看结果。复盘时间由本店业务节奏和数据条件确定，不套用统一天数。

例如，对一个没有活动、可以独立控制的会议厅，试查可以从核对活动结束后的普通照明开始。使用部门确认清场时间，工程确认控制范围，值班人员记录执行情况；临时活动回来时，按已确定的准备时间恢复。这类低风险动作适合先验证。它不能证明空调、热水或其他系统也可以照样调整。

账单变小，还要解释为什么

验证时，财务先把比较期间对齐。读表时段不同、单价或计费项目改变，都可能让账单金额变化；因此要同时看实际电量和支出，不能只对比两张账单的总额。

工程与使用部门再核对营业条件：实际入住间夜、餐饮及会议使用、营业区域、天气和设备故障是否变化。ENERGY STAR的建筑能源比较方法考虑天气和运行特征，提醒我们不能把条件不同的两段记录直接当作效率变化的证据。这里不搬用美国评分或能耗中位数作为中国酒店目标。

把整店电量除以入住间夜，可以观察一个指标，却不能让餐饮、会议和公共系统的负荷消失。客房需求下降而这些负荷保持时，每间夜分摊电量可能上升。这需要解释，不宜据此直接否定工程团队，也不能据整店电量下降直接认可节能成果。

条件差异较大、计量不足，或者同时改动多项措施时，应先补记录、延长观察，必要时请专业人员评估。短期试查只能帮助识别问题，不能自动算出净节能量。要扩大措施，还需确认效果可解释，并把恢复运行、额外人工和维护等成本纳入考虑。

节能升级，应当同时守住服务

电量减少而客人需要的服务变差，不是合格结果。出现室内环境异常、服务准备延迟、设备报警或其他超出批准条件的情况，应立即按恢复安排处理，由工程复核原因。涉及安全要求的设备和系统，不进入一般节能试查。

总经理负责跨部门协调和服务边界，工程负责技术判断及运行记录，使用部门负责准确传达需求，财务负责计量与成本口径。已有措施符合需求、记录充分且运行正常时，也无需为了“升级”再增加动作。管理升级的价值，是减少不必要运行，并让结果可以检查。

下一次经营会，先选一个低风险区域，把需求、运行、调整、恢复和验证填清楚。客流变化怎样传到设备安排上，才是节后节能管理应当补上的一步。

资料参考：美国环保署ENERGY STAR商业建筑节能措施清单、运行维护最佳实践及能源评分计算方法，2026年10月7日查阅。本文提供经营检查方法，设备调整须由本店专业人员依据实际系统和适用要求确认。
contentEn:
After Golden Week, When Guest Traffic Falls, Have Your Hotel’s Energy-Saving Measures Improved?

After the Golden Week peak, if occupied room nights, restaurant covers or meeting activity at your property begin to fall, the general manager has a useful question to ask: has the hotel’s energy operating plan changed with its business volume?

To assess whether energy-saving measures have improved, start with how the property operates. Which areas are still in use? Which equipment still starts on the peak-period schedule? Who adjusts it, and how will normal operation resume when demand returns? Each needs a clear arrangement. A lower electricity bill can prompt an investigation, but cannot alone prove that a measure works. Installing new equipment does not necessarily mean operations have improved either.

Fewer guests do not necessarily mean less equipment running

Hotel energy use is not driven by room occupancy alone. Breakfast, banquets, meetings, laundry and public areas each have operating requirements. With the same number of occupied room nights, different restaurant covers or meeting hours can produce different whole-property electricity consumption. Some systems must also maintain essential operation; more vacant rooms do not justify a proportional reduction across the board.

Suppose room demand falls after the holiday at a hotel whose meeting rooms still host consecutive events. A property-wide electricity reduction based only on room occupancy could restrict areas with active business demand. Conversely, lighting and air conditioning in unused meeting rooms may still start early on the old schedule, creating an opportunity to check for unnecessary operation. This hypothetical example explains the method; it does not describe a real property.

The general manager should first ask rooms, food-and-beverage and meeting managers to report actual usage requirements, then have engineering check equipment operating records. When changing demand does not reach the equipment schedule, energy management can remain little more than a reminder to switch off the lights.

Adjust operations before discussing investment

The US Environmental Protection Agency’s ENERGY STAR commercial-building checklist lists checking equipment left running outside operating hours, optimizing start-up and shutdown times, and equipment sequencing as low-cost measures. Its operations and maintenance guidance also emphasizes checking timer and other control settings. These provide a way to investigate; the actual adjustments must suit the property’s systems.

For a meeting room with independent controls, first check how long lighting and air conditioning actually run after an event ends. In back-of-house areas, check whether ordinary lighting is switched off as planned outside working hours. Do not inspect only what the controller says: check the actual condition on site. Where timer settings, staff actions and equipment operation disagree, adding energy-saving equipment may not solve the problem.

Before adjusting anything, define authority and operating limits. Check ordinary lighting separately from emergency lighting. Engineering should assess the operating requirements of air-conditioning, ventilation and hot-water systems; individual departments should not start or stop them on their own. Whether a load can be reduced or operating hours shortened depends on system design, ventilation, environmental maintenance, service commitments and local requirements. A central system may not support independent adjustment for a single room or area. It cannot simply copy the approach used for separately controlled equipment.

If equipment or controls need replacement, engineering should establish the technical case, finance should review the full investment cost, and the owner should decide the budget. Buying an energy-saving solution before understanding operating deviations may turn a problem that could be solved at low cost into a new investment.

An operating adjustment sheet that can be used on site

At the first post-holiday operating meeting, select one relatively low-risk area with independent controls and complete the following seven entries. The sheet organizes an investigation; it does not call for equipment shutdowns throughout the property.

Area and equipment: identify the location and equipment, whether controls are independent, and which meter measures consumption. “Save energy in the meeting area” is not specific enough.

Actual demand: the user department records activity hours, preparation time and the service conditions that must be maintained. Engineering should not treat the booking schedule as actual usage; it must also check activities added at short notice.

Existing operation: record actual start-up and shutdown times and the control method, distinguishing manual action from automatic control. If records are missing, collect measurements first. Do not enter “previously running all day” from memory.

Proposed adjustment: engineering specifies which setting will change, why the change is feasible and which equipment will remain unchanged. Where possible, change only one main operating arrangement in each trial so the result can be interpreted.

Execution and restoration: identify who implements and approves the adjustment, how long normal operation takes to restore, and how new bookings or last-minute activities will be communicated. Restoring service should not depend on finding someone at short notice to unlock a room or start equipment.

Verification records: list the relevant electricity consumption, usage hours, weather, observed operating condition, service issues and resources required to restore operation. Without a submeter, note that whole-property data includes other business loads.

Reversal and review: specify what observations require the original arrangement to be restored, who can act immediately and when results will be reviewed. Set the review timing according to the property’s business cycle and data availability, rather than a universal number of days.

For example, a trial in an independently controlled meeting room with no scheduled activity could begin by checking ordinary lighting after an event. The user department confirms when the room is cleared, engineering confirms the control scope, and duty staff record implementation. If a last-minute event is added, restore operation within the agreed preparation time. A low-risk action of this kind is suitable for initial verification. It does not establish that air-conditioning, hot water or other systems can be adjusted in the same way.

A smaller bill still needs an explanation

For verification, finance should first align the comparison periods. Different meter-reading intervals, unit prices or billing components can change the amount payable. Compare actual electricity consumption and expenditure together, rather than just the totals on two bills.

Engineering and user departments should then check operating conditions: actual occupied room nights, restaurant and meeting usage, areas open for business, weather and equipment faults. ENERGY STAR’s building-energy comparison methodology considers weather and operating characteristics. It reminds us that two periods with different conditions cannot be treated directly as evidence of an efficiency change. US scores or median consumption figures are not being adopted here as targets for Chinese hotels.

Dividing whole-property electricity consumption by occupied room nights provides one indicator, but does not remove the loads associated with restaurants, meetings and shared systems. If room demand falls while those loads remain, electricity allocated to each occupied room night may rise. That needs explanation; it should not automatically discredit engineering. Nor should a fall in whole-property consumption automatically establish that an energy-saving measure has worked.

Where conditions differ substantially, metering is insufficient or several measures change at once, first improve the records, extend observation and seek professional assessment where necessary. A short trial can identify issues, but does not automatically quantify net energy savings. Before extending a measure, confirm that its effect can be explained and include the costs of restoring operation, additional labour and maintenance.

Better energy management must also protect service

Lower consumption coupled with poorer service is not an acceptable result. If indoor conditions become abnormal, service preparation is delayed, equipment alarms occur or other conditions exceed the approved limits, act immediately under the restoration plan and have engineering investigate. Equipment and systems subject to safety requirements are excluded from a general energy-saving trial.

The general manager coordinates departments and defines service boundaries; engineering owns technical judgement and operating records; user departments communicate demand accurately; finance owns the metering and cost basis. If existing measures match demand, records are sufficient and systems operate normally, there is no need to add actions simply to demonstrate an upgrade. Better management reduces unnecessary operation and makes the result open to inspection.

At the next operating meeting, select one low-risk area and document demand, operation, adjustment, restoration and verification. Connecting changing guest demand to equipment operation is the step post-holiday energy management needs to address.

References: US Environmental Protection Agency ENERGY STAR Checklists of Energy-Saving Measures, Operation and Maintenance Best Practices, and How the 1–100 ENERGY STAR Score is Calculated, accessed 7 October 2026. This article provides an operating review method. The property’s qualified staff must confirm equipment adjustments against its actual systems and applicable requirements.
author: MarvelBros C&T
